feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. Your entity0 cites iteration 7 as a ±0.03 design, but the outcome table records iteration 7 at x = ±0.036 with kd 0.35. The 97.7 to 160.5 gain came from raising kd 0.25 to 0.35 on the same geometry, so the reach change you attribute it to was not tested. Evidence: iteration 5 (±0.036, kd 0.15) scored 52.4, and iteration 4 (±0.03, kd 0.15) scored 52.2, so reach was neutral at kd 0.15. I have therefore raced the verified iteration 7 geometry at ±0.036 to protect the best known score. Next race: if the score holds near 160 with oval completions kept, the damping is confirmed and the next single-variable test is the reach or wheel_track. If the score falls below about 130 on the same controller, check for run-to-run variation before drawing any geometry conclusion.
requested_changes: Keep the outer sensors at x = ±0.036 with y = 0.04, 15 mm spacing for the middle three, and sensor_size 0.016. Evidence: iteration 7 (±0.036, kd 0.35) scored 160.5, the best raced result, and reach was neutral at kd 0.15 (iterations 4 and 5).

If you still want to test ±0.03, do it as one change against iteration 7 (reach only, kd 0.35 kept), so the score difference can be attributed. Evidence: iteration 6 (±0.036, kd 0.25) scored 97.7, and iteration 7 showed kd, not reach, drove the large gain.

If slalom line_loss_events stays at 1 or more with slalom progress below 0.16 after the damping, test wheel_track 0.14 from 0.12 with nothing else changed. Evidence: iterations 3 to 7 never changed the turn rate per wheel, and slalom line loss has stayed at 1 or above throughout.
